Hi Alicia —

Thanks again for the time earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a clear verification path versus the hyperscaler alternatives you mentioned. High-level differentiators we heard you care about: predictable SLOs, graceful failover across regions, transparent rate-limiting, and predictable cost per token under sustained throughput.

What we propose as a short verification plan (we can run in a staging workspace we control):
- Test A: Controlled failover — simulate region outage and measure failover latency, tail error rate, and request continuity (30m blast).
- Test B: Burst & throttling — 1k concurrent sessions ramp to 10k rps for 5m to validate rate limit behavior, token queuing, and 503 vs 429 surface area.
- Test C: Error-budget consumption — run synthetic load until 0.1% error budget consumed to validate alerting and automatic fallback to compatible model variants.
- Data to collect: p50/p95/p99 latency, success rate, error codes, KV cache hit-rate, token counts, and per-tenant rate-limit events.

I've attached a rough SLO matrix (redwood-slo-matrix-20260408.pdf) and the recording from today's demo. If this plan looks OK, could you confirm: (1) preferred windows (US business hours preferred), (2) whether we can run these tests against a staging copy of your integration, and (3) a contact for procurement/security if we need to share signed test tokens?

Next steps I recommend:
- You confirm test priority and timing.
- We schedule a 30-min pre-test sync (technical) with our SRE/SE to walk through the harness.
- We share a small runbook + temporary test API keys and a dashboard link for live results.

Thanks — I'll loop in Vivek (SRE lead) and Karthik (solutions) so you have technical owners on our side.

Best,

Alicia — thanks, noted. Below are the SLO targets and a tentative schedule for the pre-test sync.

Proposed SLO targets to validate (what our service guarantees under Dedicated/reserved capacity):
- Availability: 99.95% (measured as per-tenant 5xx error rate + connectivity failures).
- Tail latency: p95 < 220ms, p99 < 480ms for short prompts (<=256 tokens) on Dedicated; hosted can vary.
- Cold-start tail: < 1s additional for a warmed pool; cold-starts may be higher for model spin-up.
- Rate-limiting: per-tenant token leaky-bucket with burst allowance; sustained rate over quota will produce 429 and token throttling rather than 503.

Tentative pre-test sync windows (30 min):
- Mon 2026-04-12 10:00-10:30 PT
- Tue 2026-04-13 13:00-13:30 PT

Test harness notes:
- We'll provide a shared Grafana dashboard and a temporary API key with scoped rate limits.
- We need an IP allowlist for the traffic generator (we'll provide the CIDR block).
- For the failover test we will orchestrate a regional failover and measure how long requests return to normal across our routing layers; we aim to minimize request loss by falling back to compatible model variants automatically (this is a Redwood behavior we demonstrated).

If that looks good I can lock Mon 4/12 10:00 PT for the pre-test sync. If security/procurement needs a contract-first flow, Tom, please advise.

Sean

Hi Alicia / Sean —

Quick technical notes and acceptance criteria from SRE side so your team can validate results:

1) Failover behavior (Test A)
- What we'll do: withdraw one region from the routing pool for 10 minutes and observe per-request routing fallback.
- Acceptance: >=95% of in-flight requests should complete (either against primary or fallback variant). Total user-visible request loss <0.05% during the window. Failover convergence to new route < 90s for majority of traffic.

2) Burst & throttling (Test B)
- Model of rate limiting: per-tenant token bucket with leaky drain; burst tokens permit short spikes, sustained over-quota triggers 429 with a Retry-After header.
- Acceptance: no silent 503s produced by our queueing; overall request success rate >= 99.5% at the agreed sustained rate; 429s should be instrumented for your dashboard.

3) Error-budget scenario (Test C - optional)
- We'll run an injected fault for short windows to validate alerting and automatic fallback to a lower-cost model variant.
- Acceptance: automated rollback or model-variant fallback executed within 2 minutes of threshold breach; post-mitigation success rate >= 99%.

Data & access:
- We'll share a Grafana link (read-only) and a CloudWatch export snapshot for the test window.
- We require a staging API endpoint and a pointer to where masked traces/logs should be written.
- Test API key will be rate-limited and expire automatically.

Operational caveats:
- If you run the burst test from an on-prem generator across NAT, please ensure TCP connections are long-lived for better measurement of p99.
- For the failover test, if your staging endpoint is behind a strict firewall, provide a temporary allowlist (we'll provide our CIDR blocks).

I'll attach a short runbook and the test script snippets to the shared Drive link. Sean — I'll plan to run Test A first, then Test B the following day; we should hold Test C until after we've validated instrumentation.

--
